page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory sizing is configured in a low-memory profile of 128 GB RAM, providing 2.0 GB of system memory per vCPU. Hardware instruction support features AVX-512 with VNNI, along with cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached block storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capabilities, with multi-core tests consistently ranking in the top 25 percentile. The instance achieved 61,847.21 in stress-ng multi-core and 16,569.0 in Geekbench multi-core workloads, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 60,731.27. Memory throughput on large un-cached blocks reached 292.88 GB/sec for reads and 135.25 GB/sec for writes. Workloads involving code compilation via Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving (53.15 GB/sec) perform in the upper performance tier. In contrast, single-core benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1671.0) and single-threaded gzip compression remain in the middle 50 percentile.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio minimizes unneeded memory overhead for compute-dense scenarios. It allows workloads requiring high thread concurrency to scale without paying the cost premium associated with standard 1:4 general-purpose memory allocations. Conversely, absence of local scratch disks requires budgeting for network storage IOPS, and execution of large 70B parameter LLM inference yields lower throughput due to memory footprint constraints. The D64ls_v5 is well positioned for software build farms, parallel batch processing, batch encryption, CI/CD pipelines, and high-concurrency web microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine designed for high-concurrency workloads requiring a reduced memory footprint. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores with hyper-threading) and 128 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. It supports AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and VAES vector extensions, while omitting local storage and hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate strong multi-threaded execution, placing in the top 25 percent for multi-core stress testing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, software compilation, and static web throughput. Single-thread execution and cached operations fall within average tiers. By eliminating redundant memory overhead and local ephemeral drives, the D64ls_v5 provides a lean compute environment optimized for batch computing, CI/CD build environments, multi-threaded worker pools, and scalable web servers.
